notYet: Not yet part of Sardinia and the Tyrrhenian

stages.name: Italic & native
stages.desc: Latins, Sabines, Umbrians, Samnites, and Sicily's Sikels, Sikans and Elymians

stages.name: Nuragic
stages.desc: Sardinian communities of the stone towers (nuraghi)

stages.name: Phoenician settlement
stages.desc: Coastal trading towns founded by Phoenicians from the Levant

states.name: Cosenza
timeline: Italic (Oenotrian) villages
Achaeans found Sybaris, soon the richest city of the west
Kroton destroys Sybaris

states.name: Reggio Calabria
timeline: Italic villages at the toe of Italy
Chalcidians found Rhegion on the Strait of Messina

states.name: Vibo Valentia
timeline: Italic villages of the Tyrrhenian coast
Lokrians found Hipponion

states.name: Salerno
timeline: Italic villages; an Etruscan-linked settlement at Pontecagnano
Greeks from Sybaris found Poseidonia (Paestum)
Phocaean refugees from Alalia found Elea (Velia)

states.name: Naples
timeline: Oscan-speaking villages around the Bay of Naples
Euboean Greeks settle Pithekoussai on Ischia, then Cumae

states.name: Caserta
timeline: Italic villages of the Campanian plain
Capua flourishes as the chief Etruscan city of Campania

states.name: Latina
timeline: Latin and, later, Volscian villages

states.name: Rome
timeline: Latin villages on the hills by the Tiber; Etruscan Caere to the north
Traditional date of the founding of Rome
Rome under Etruscan kings, beginning with Tarquinius Priscus
The last king is expelled and Rome becomes a republic

states.name: Viterbo
timeline: Villanovan, then Etruscan Tarquinia and Vulci

states.name: Grosseto
timeline: Villanovan, then Etruscan Vetulonia and Roselle

states.name: Livorno
timeline: Etruscan Populonia, smelting iron from Elba

states.name: Pisa
timeline: Etruscan Volterra and Pisa

states.name: Trapani
timeline: Elymian and Sikan lands of western Sicily
Phoenicians settle on the island of Motya
Greek Selinus is founded on the south coast, beside the Phoenician west
Carthage crushes Dorieus at Eryx and shields the Phoenician west

states.name: Messina
timeline: Sikel lands of north-eastern Sicily
Euboean Greeks found Naxos, then Zancle on the Strait

states.name: Palermo
timeline: Sikan and Elymian hill villages
Phoenician harbours at Panormos (Palermo) and Solus
Greek Himera is founded on the coast to the east
The Phoenician towns fall under Carthaginian protection

states.name: Agrigento
timeline: Sikan villages of the south coast
Gela founds Akragas

states.name: Caltanissetta
timeline: Sikan and Sikel hill country
Rhodians and Cretans found Gela

states.name: Ragusa
timeline: Sikel villages of the Hyblaean hills
Syracuse founds Kamarina

states.name: Syracuse
timeline: Sikel villages of the south-east
Corinthians found Syracuse

states.name: Catania
timeline: Sikel villages below Mount Etna
Greeks from Naxos found Leontinoi and Katane

states.name: Carbonia-Iglesias
timeline: Nuragic communities among the copper, lead and silver ores of the Sulcis
Phoenicians found Sulci on the island of Sant'Antioco
Sulci builds the hilltop stronghold of Monte Sirai
Sardinians defeat Malchus' Carthaginian army; Monte Sirai is attacked
Carthage takes Sulci and refortifies Monte Sirai

states.name: Sassari
timeline: Nuragic north-west: towers, villages and the harbour village of Sant'Imbenia
Phoenician and Euboean traders visit Sant'Imbenia, near Alghero

states.name: Nuoro
timeline: Nuragic highlands of the Barbagia, with sacred wells and sanctuaries
The mountain interior remains outside Carthaginian rule

states.name: Olbia-Tempio
timeline: Nuragic Gallura, a granite country of towers and giants' tombs

states.name: Oristano
timeline: Nuragic heartland of the Sinis peninsula and the Gulf of Oristano
The stone giants of Mont'e Prama stand over a cemetery (date debated)
Phoenician Tharros and Othoca dominate the gulf
Carthage conquers the west coast; Hasdrubal falls in the fighting

states.name: Medio Campidano
timeline: Nuragic towers of the Marmilla, including Su Nuraxi of Barumini
Carthaginian control reaches the grain plains of the Campidano

states.name: Cagliari
timeline: Nuragic villages and towers around the Gulf of Cagliari
Phoenicians settle at Nora; the Nora Stone names Sardinia
Karalis (Cagliari) grows into a Phoenician harbour town
Carthaginian armies under Mago's sons take control of the south

states.name: Ogliastra
timeline: Nuragic communities of the eastern mountains and coast

states.name: Enna
timeline: Sikel and Sikan hill towns of the interior

states.name: Benevento
timeline: Samnite hill country

states.name: Siena
timeline: Etruscan Chiusi and the hill country of Siena

states.name: Rieti
timeline: Sabine villages of the hills

states.name: Terni
timeline: Umbrian villages along the Nera

states.name: Frosinone
timeline: Hernican and Volscian hill towns

states.name: Avellino
timeline: Samnite hill country of the Irpini

events.title: Land of the towers
events.text: Nuragic Sardinians have raised thousands of dry-stone towers, such as Su Nuraxi at Barumini.

events.title: Sacred wells
events.text: Well temples such as Santa Cristina, built with finely cut stone, serve Nuragic water cults.

events.title: Sardinian bronzes in Vulci
events.text: A Villanovan tomb at Vulci holds Sardinian bronze figurines, a sign of early trade across the sea.

events.title: Sant'Imbenia
events.text: Phoenician and Euboean traders work beside Nuragic villagers at this harbour village near Alghero.

events.title: The Nora Stone
events.text: A Phoenician inscription at Nora, the oldest in the western Mediterranean, names Sardinia.

events.title: Carthage founded
events.text: By tradition, settlers from Tyre found Carthage on the coast of North Africa.

events.title: The stone giants
events.text: Life-size and larger stone warriors, archers and boxers are carved at Mont'e Prama; their date is debated.

events.title: Pithekoussai
events.text: Euboean Greeks set up a trading settlement on the island of Ischia.

events.title: Sulci founded
events.text: Phoenicians found Sulci on Sant'Antioco, near the island's richest ores.

events.title: Rome founded
events.text: The traditional date of the founding of Rome, then a cluster of Latin villages.

events.title: Motya
events.text: Phoenicians settle on a small island off western Sicily.

events.title: Monte Sirai
events.text: Sulci builds a hilltop stronghold overlooking the plain of the Sulcis.

events.title: Cumae
events.text: Greeks from Pithekoussai found Cumae on the mainland.

events.title: Naxos
events.text: Euboean Greeks found Naxos, the first Greek colony in Sicily.

events.title: Syracuse
events.text: Corinthian settlers found Syracuse.

events.title: Tharros
events.text: Phoenicians settle at Tharros on the Sinis peninsula, near Mont'e Prama.

events.title: Sybaris
events.text: Achaean Greeks found Sybaris, later famous for its wealth.

events.title: Rhegion
events.text: Chalcidians found Rhegion on the Strait of Messina.

events.title: Karalis
events.text: A Phoenician town grows on the Gulf of Cagliari.

events.title: Gela
events.text: Rhodian and Cretan colonists found Gela on Sicily's south coast.

events.title: Etruscan princes
events.text: Rich tombs at Caere, like the Regolini-Galassi tomb, show Etruscan wealth from metals and trade.

events.title: Himera
events.text: Greeks found Himera on Sicily's north coast, near the Phoenician towns.

events.title: Selinus
events.text: Megarian Greeks found Selinus, the westernmost Greek city in Sicily.

events.title: Etruscan king of Rome
events.text: Tarquinius Priscus, of Etruscan origin, becomes king of Rome.

events.title: Giants broken?
events.text: One theory dates the smashing of the Mont'e Prama statues to the late 7th century; others place it later.

events.title: Poseidonia
events.text: Greeks from Sybaris found Poseidonia, later Paestum.

events.title: Populonia's iron
events.text: Etruscan Populonia smelts iron ore shipped from Elba.

events.title: Akragas
events.text: Gela founds Akragas, which becomes one of the great Greek cities.

events.title: Pentathlos defeated
events.text: A Greek expedition to Lilybaeum is driven off by Elymians and Phoenicians.

events.title: Alalia founded
events.text: Phocaean Greeks settle at Alalia on Corsica, facing Sardinia.

events.title: Malchus defeated
events.text: A Carthaginian army under Malchus is beaten by the Sardinians; he is exiled and besieges Carthage.

events.title: Battle of Alalia
events.text: Carthaginian and Etruscan fleets fight the Phocaeans, who win but abandon Corsica.

events.title: Elea (Velia)
events.text: Phocaean refugees from Alalia found Elea on the Campanian coast.

events.title: Battle of Cumae
events.text: The Greeks of Cumae under Aristodemus repel an Etruscan army.

events.title: Mago's sons invade
events.text: Hasdrubal and Hamilcar lead a Carthaginian conquest; burnt layers mark Monte Sirai and other sites.

events.title: Hasdrubal falls
events.text: The Carthaginian general Hasdrubal dies of wounds fighting in Sardinia.

events.title: Sybaris destroyed
events.text: The army of Kroton destroys Sybaris.

events.title: Dorieus at Eryx
events.text: Carthage and its allies destroy a Spartan prince's colony in western Sicily.

events.title: Roman Republic
events.text: The Romans expel Tarquinius Superbus and found the Republic.

events.title: Treaty with Carthage
events.text: Rome's first treaty with Carthage lets Romans trade in Sardinia only under Carthaginian officials.

chartNote: Share of the area of the mapped provinces (today's boundaries), by the people who dominated each one. A simplification: Phoenician towns stood beside Nuragic villages and Greek cities beside native ones, and many dates are approximate or debated.
